title: GIS-BASED GROUNDWATER QUALITY ASSESSMENT AND IRRIGATION SUITABILITY FOR SUSTAINABLE WATER MANAGEMENT IN BAHR AL-NAJAF, IRAQ

GIS-BASED GROUNDWATER QUALITY ASSESSMENT AND IRRIGATION SUITABILITY FOR SUSTAINABLE WATER MANAGEMENT IN BAHR AL-NAJAF, IRAQ

ABSTRACT

With the advancement of agricultural technology, there is an increasing need to assess groundwater wells and ensure that they are adequate for irrigation and farming. The hydrogeological characteristics of groundwater, including its chemical and physical constituents, must be present in modest amounts to guaranty water suitability. This study will evaluate the efficacy of groundwater wells in the Najaf Basin region to confirm their suitability for agricultural use and crop irrigation by calculating modeling efficiency metrics. In addition, GIS data from 72 groundwater wells in the Najaf Basin of Iraq were analyzed between 2025 and 2026. In particular, the PS, SSP, RSC, and SAR metrics showed that 100% of the wells had good ratings. With the exception of six wells that exceeded the indicators’ permissible levels and require local monitoring and treatment, the KI indicators revealed an efficiency and quality rate of 91.7% for a total of 72 groundwater wells. The current study also showed the value and effectiveness of Geographic Information System (GIS) technology in planning and creating maps for the geographical distribution of all water quality indicators for artesian wells in the research region. The findings of this study showed a good agreement with the most current comparative studies. This research recommends creating programs for continuous monitoring and supervision of well water quality indicators in addition to conducting studies specific to each season in order to monitor and assess changes in the hydrogeological characteristics of wells in the Najaf Sea region. The research also recommends that wells with high KI values be regularly checked, treated with substances to reduce concentrations, and mixed with other substances.
